clue.text: Gutless benefactor, one criticising Nobel, by the sound of it!

definitions.text: Nobel, by the sound of it!
definitions.note: said aloud, Nobel is 'no bell': a house without a bell needs another way to announce callers

indicators.note: gutless means with the insides removed, so the middle letter of the benefactor word goes

parts.note: a benefactor is a donor, one who gives money
someone who criticises knocks, so is a knocker

explanation.surface: A donor's courage is questioned while someone sneers at the Nobel Prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutless' strips the central N from DONOR. The definition is a pun: Nobel heard as 'no bell', and what hangs on a door with no bell is this.
explanation.definitionFit: Where a house has no bell, visitors rap with the metal fitting on the front door instead, so it stands in for the missing bell.

clue.text: Upset kid to deal with US president

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word for kid is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to kid is to tease, to rag
to field a question is to deal with it

explanation.surface: A child upset over handling an American leader.
explanation.definitionFit: James Garfield was the twentieth President of the United States, assassinated in 1881.

clue.text: Unknown element with carbon in mineral

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns; here z

indicators.note: in says the carbon letter goes inside the element

parts.note: iron is a chemical element
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson: an unidentified element combined with carbon inside a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Zircon is a silicate mineral, zirconium silicate, used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Solver always ignorant, perhaps

parts.note: the setter addresses the solver as you
someone always ignorant will never know

explanation.surface: A cheeky jab at the person doing the puzzle: perhaps you are permanently clueless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom used to admit that something might just happen, much like maybe.

clue.text: Having stopped short, continue climbing to rescue old cat

indicators.note: to rescue is to take in and hold safe, so the letter for old goes inside
in a down clue climbing reads the letters upwards, i.e. backwards
stopped short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to continue is to resume

explanation.surface: A climber stops, carries on upwards and saves an elderly cat stuck in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: RESUME cut short is RESUM; 'climbing' turns it to MUSER, and 'to rescue' puts O inside after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat kept or valued for catching mice.

clue.text: See 4
Area regularly cleared, bordering Asian country

indicators.note: bordering means lying on both sides of, so the two letters wrap round the Asian
clearing every other letter of the word for area leaves alternate letters

parts.note: an Omani is a person from Oman, in Asia

explanation.surface: A cleared zone along a border with an Asian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly cleared' keeps the even letters R and A of 'Area'; 'bordering' puts them round OMANI.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a nation in south-eastern Europe on the Black Sea.

clue.text: Briefly, nation of bandits starts turning over European city

indicators.note: turning over means flipping the whole string so it reads backwards
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the nation is dropped

parts.note: Angola is an African nation

indicators.note: the starts of the two words 'of bandits' are their first letters

explanation.surface: A lawless country of brigands is overturning things in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: ANGOL plus OB (starts of 'of bandits') is ANGOLOB; 'turning over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bologna is a city in northern Italy, capital of Emilia-Romagna.

clue.text: Extra money gained — it's not there for teacher

indicators.note: not there says the letters of it are missing from the money word

parts.note: money gained beyond what was spent is profit
the word it, with 's as the verb is

explanation.surface: Someone notes that bonus earnings never reach the teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Prof is short for professor, a university teacher.

clue.text: Probing farm animal, point injected into swine with a sharp instrument

indicators.note: probing means pushing into, so what follows goes inside the farm animal

parts.note: a cow is a farm animal

indicators.note: injected into means put inside, so the point goes within swine

parts.note: swine here are pigs
N is a compass point, north

explanation.surface: A gruesome farmyard scene: livestock and pigs jabbed with a sharp tool.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions: 'injected into' puts the point inside swine, then 'Probing' sends that string, with A added, into the farm animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fine-bladed saw in a frame, used for cutting curves in wood: a sharp cutting tool.

clue.text: Uplifting painting of chief about right for artist's work

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means raising up, so everything reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting

indicators.note: about means around, so the chief word goes round the letter for right

parts.note: top means chief, as in top dog

explanation.surface: An inspiring picture of the boss, flattering for an artist's collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R just after the first letter of the chief word, so the whole string read upward begins PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a collection of an artist's pieces, gathered to show what they can do.

clue.text: See 13
Puzzling arrangement with sheep leaving, heading north around hot country

indicators.note: around says the reversed letters go round the letter for hot
in a down clue heading north means going upwards, so it reads backwards
leaving means going out, so the sheep's letters are removed

parts.note: an anagram is a puzzling arrangement of letters
a ram is a male sheep
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A puzzling arrangement with sheep departing, travelling north to somewhere hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzling arrangement' is a definition of the word anagram, not an anagram signal; 'heading north' reverses what is left, and 'around' wraps it round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a West African nation, formerly the Gold Coast.

clue.text: With sailor's termination, pine perhaps about death for colourful character on board?

indicators.note: the termination of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: about means around, so the tree word wraps round death

parts.note: a pine is an example of an evergreen tree
an end is a death

explanation.surface: A cryptic portrait of a sailor's demise near a pine, for some vivid figure aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship but means a board game: Cluedo's suspects are named by colours, and this clergyman is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The clergyman suspect in the board game Cluedo carries a colour in his name, so he is a colourful board-game character.

clue.text: Tender resignation finally, sure to be sacked

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of resignation
sacked here means plundered and wrecked, so the letters of sure are thrown about

explanation.surface: An employee's resignation letter ends in being fired, sure enough.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend someone who is ill is to care for them in the medical way, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Land, safe ground for one shelled on the beach?

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailors reach land and safe ground after being shelled on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled on the beach' evokes bombardment, but means a crustacean with a shell found there.
explanation.definitionFit: This small hopping crustacean lives on sandy shores; it has a hard shell-like covering, so is a shelled beach creature.

clue.text: See 17
Happy getting rich, transferred from a central bank?

parts.note: feeling up is feeling happy
loaded is slang for very rich

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful at getting wealthy, the money moved from the Bank of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central bank' suggests finance; it is a central data store, a server.
explanation.definitionFit: Files sent up to a server are moved onto it, and a server acts as a shared central store of data.

clue.text: Surprise to arrive at a literary festival?

definitions.meaning: an unexpected event, an idiom for a shock outcome

definitions.text: to arrive at a literary festival?
definitions.meaning: read literally, to appear in order to attend an event about books

explanation.surface: A writer turning up unannounced at a book festival.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from bookmakers' ledgers, describes a result nobody expected, an upset.

clue.text: See 17 across
Engineers admitting everyone in China destined never to meet

indicators.note: in says the whole group sits inside the word for china

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china (plate) means mate, so a pal

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so everyone goes inside the engineers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Engineers bring everyone into China, though they are fated never to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' = mate, so pal. RE is the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that run side by side at a constant distance never intersect however far they extend.

clue.text: Medicinal plant — someone taking heart from therapy, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say marks that the result is heard, not spelt

parts.note: the heart of therapy is its middle letter R, and someone taking it is an R nicker, one who nicks (steals) it

explanation.surface: A patient drawing courage from treatment asks about a herbal remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: One who nicks R, the heart of 'therapy', is an 'R nicker', which in non-rhotic British speech sounds like the plant; nick is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnica is a mountain plant of the daisy family whose extract is used to treat bruises.

clue.text: Audible, quiet man

indicators.note: audible says the word for quiet is heard, not written

parts.note: peace means quiet, calm

explanation.surface: A man who is quiet yet can be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess and draughts each counter or figure on the board is called a man.

clue.text: Pattern of Scots crossing cold lake

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the pattern goes round the letter for cold

parts.note: plaid is the Scottish tartan pattern
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A tartan design spread across a chilly Scottish loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lake' looks like part of the scene but is the definition: Lake Placid in New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Placid is a lake in New York's Adirondacks, home of two Winter Olympics.

clue.text: Writers given non-alcoholic drink after a port in Florida

indicators.note: after says the drink comes after the letter a

parts.note: pens are writing implements
cola is a soft drink

explanation.surface: Authors handed soft drinks after arriving at a Florida harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensacola is a port city on the Gulf coast of the Florida panhandle.

clue.text: See 25
Some alligator fed fish

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An alligator was given some fish to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe, or ide, is a freshwater fish of the carp family, often kept golden in ponds.

clue.text: See 15
See 1
Happy parasite was ahead of salmon

parts.note: a tick is a blood-sucking parasite
to have led is to have been ahead
salmon is a pinkish-orange colour, here pink

explanation.surface: A parasite got in front of a salmon in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salmon' suggests the fish; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very pleased indeed, so it serves as an adjective for being delighted.
